rationale:
structural: The structural obligations in `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection` are the three prescribed signatures, plus the requirement that a selection is an owned `OutlineContent` that shares the original snapshot, does no further file read, and outlives the original handle. The three roots implement these.

- `select`: `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#impl[OutlineContent]/fn[select]` has the signature `pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>`. It resolves the selector against `self.snapshot.outline.items`, which is the retained outline. It then returns a new `Self` whose `snapshot` is `self.snapshot.clone()`, an `Arc<Snapshot>` clone. That clone shares the source and outline without re-reading the file, and it keeps working after the original handle is dropped. An alternative that re-read the file or copied the source would violate this clause, and this code does neither. Errors for an invalid, missing or ambiguous selector come from `selection_error`. The `line` interchangeability rule is checked through the structural hash comparison. Both behaviors are governed by the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`, which supply context only.
- `id`: `impl[OutlineContent]/fn[id]` has the signature `pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineData` and returns the stored `id`.
- `text`: `impl[OutlineContent]/fn[text]` has the signature `pub fn text(&self) -> &str`. It slices the shared `snapshot.source` by the selected item's span, so the text is unredacted and includes attached source.

The supporting declarations need no separate reference. `struct[OutlineContent]` holds `snapshot: Arc<Snapshot>`, and `struct[Snapshot]` holds `source: Arc<str>`. Both are types used by the marked items and are already referenced by `requirements.sdk.outlines.outline_file.lifetime`. The `item()` helper is reached from `text`. No structural obligation is left without an implementation root.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover every behavioral obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection`. Each test below is marked `{test}` for the requirement.

- **Resolving a selector from the root and returning an owned item handle.**
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` selects every outline item. It asserts that the text equals the item's span and that the structural hash matches.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` selects Markdown items through nested, encoded, `#N` and anonymous selectors.
  - `css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent` does the same for CSS.
  - `selecting_multipart_impls_and_literal_slashes_preserves_label_boundaries` selects multipart `impl[...]` labels and `%2F`-encoded slashes.
  - `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` and `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` select plain-text `line@hash` items.
  - In `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits`, `select("")` returns the root, checked with `OutlineData::root` and the full text.
- **`id()` and `text()` of the selected item.**
  - `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` asserts `selected_again.id()` equals the id and the text is `second`.
  - `formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans` asserts that the selected `text()` keeps the raw token, while `format()` shows `[REDACTED:GitHub Token]`. This covers "original text before redaction".
- **Sharing the source snapshot and fingerprinting rules.**
  - `explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme` checks that a selected item keeps the language and the `custom-v2` scheme. It checks that selecting from a path-loaded handle and from a source-supplied handle gives equal fingerprints. It also checks that a `custom-v3` language gives a different fingerprint.
  - The Rust and Markdown tests assert `std::ptr::eq(selected.outline(), contents.outline())`, so the outline is shared.
- **No additional file read, and usability after the original handle is dropped.** `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` calls `drop(file)` and then rewrites the file on disk. It then asserts that `selected_again.text()` and the fingerprint are unchanged. It also selects `""` from `selected` after the edit and gets the original full text. A fresh `from_id` fails, which shows the file really changed.
- **Selector-syntax rules, including interchangeable identical plain-text lines.** `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` and the `alpha` selection in `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` cover this. Identical lines have equal selectors, and selecting one succeeds.
- **Errors for invalid, missing and ambiguous selections.**
  - `missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors` asserts an error for the malformed selector `fn[` and for the missing item `fn[absent]`.
  - `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` asserts an "ambiguous" error for duplicate `part` and `line` items with differing hashes.
  - The CSS test asserts an error for the unnumbered duplicate `rule[a%20b]`.
  - The multipart and Markdown test asserts an error for `impl[Thing%2Fcore::fmt::Display]` and `section[A/B]`.

The requirement does not say how to distinguish a malformed selector from a missing item, so I found no gap there. The detailed selector grammar and the error rules belong to `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`. They are cited context and I did not reassess them here.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineData;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. In a multipart label such as `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `/` separates
name parts. A slash within one part is encoded as `%2F`. Line numbers MUST NOT
form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
The outline API makes a best effort to recover from parse errors.
File-read and unrecoverable parsing failures return errors, distinct from
successful contents for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that
language's parsing rules.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` also returns an error.
